wiki_en.trecho: | • Capital of | Sakha Republic[2] | | • Capital of | city of republic significance of Yakutsk[1] | Yakutsk[a] is the capital and largest city of Sakha, Russia, located about 450 km (280 mi) south of the Arctic Circle. Yakutsk has an average annual temperature of −8.0 °C (17.6 °F),[9] winter high temperatures consistently well below −20 °C (−4 °F), and a record low of −64.4 °C (−83.9 °F) has been recorded.[10] As a result, Yakutsk is the coldest city of over 200,000 people in the world (though a number of smaller towns in that region (and the Northwest Territories and Nunavut[b]) are colder).[11] Yakutsk is also the largest city located in continuous permafrost; the only other large city is Norilsk, also in Siberia.[12] Yakutsk is in the Central Yakutian Lowland and is a major port on the Lena River. In 2012, the reconstruction of Yakutsk Airport was completed, transforming it into a modern international airport complex.[23] In the 2010s, the Amur–Yakutsk Mainline was extended directly to the vicinity of the city (terminating at Nizhny Bestyakh station on the opposite bank of the Lena River), which qualitatively transformed the logistics of cargo delivery.[24] In 2010, the M. Summers are sunny, warm and occasionally hot (though short), with daily maximum temperatures exceeding +30 °C (86 °F), making the seasonal temperature differences for the region the greatest in the world at 102 °C (184 °F).[26] The lowest temperature recorded in Yakutsk was −64.4 °C (−83.9 °F) on February 5, 1891, and the highest temperatures +38.4 °C (101.1 °F) on July 17, 2011, and +38.3 °C (100.9 °F) on July 15, 1942. The hottest month in records going back to 1834 has been July 1894, with a mean of +23.2 °C (73.8 °F),[10] and the coldest, January 1900, which averaged −51.4 °C (−60.5 °F).[27] Yakutsk is the largest city in the world with an average winter temperature of below −30 °C (−22 °F).[citation needed] The primary economic activity stems from mining activities in the region, particularly coal, gold, and diamonds, with multiple mining companies having set up their headquarters in the city.[32] Precious stones and metals, particularly diamonds, as well as coal, are Yakutsk's major exports.[32] The export volume was $5.55 billion in 2021, making it the 16th largest out of eighty-five of Russia's federal subjects, although it contracted sharply (under $1 billion) in 2022.[33] Yakutsk Airport is the main airport,[32] and Yakutia Airlines has its head office in the city, operating flights between Yakutsk and other main Russian cities.[34] There is also a branch of the Russian Academy of Sciences, which contains, among other things, the Institute of Cosmophysical Research, which runs the Yakutsk Extensive Air Shower installation (one of the largest cosmic-ray detector arrays in the world), and the Melnikov Permafrost Institute, founded in 1960 with the aim of solving the serious and costly problems associated with construction of buildings on frozen soil.

wiki_pt.trecho: Iacutusque, Iacútseque ou Iakutsk (russo:  Якутск; IPA: [jɪˈkutsk]; em iacuto:  Дьокуускай, Jokūskaĭ, pronunciado [ɟokuːskaj]) é uma cidade da Rússia, capital da região da República de Saca (Iacútia), na Sibéria Oriental. Possui 303 863 habitantes, sendo, assim, a maior cidade do mundo construída sobre o permafrost — um tipo de solo típico da região do Ártico e que fica permanentemente congelado — e é uma região remota com mais de 122 km² de área. Iacutusque é umas das cidades mais frias do mundo. A cidade possui temperaturas muito variadas, tendo verões e invernos longos por torno de quatro meses. Iacutusque, juntamente com as cidades russas de Oimiakon e Verkhoiansk, são as únicas cidades no mundo onde a amplitude térmica pode variar mais que 100 °C. O clima da cidade de Iacutusque é subártico extremo (Dwd), apesar de a latitude ser 62° e a elevação ser menos de 200 metros de altitude. Foi fundada como um forte cossaco em 25 de setembro de 1632 e não foi realmente uma cidade até que fossem descobertas as reservas de ouro siberianas no fim do século XIX. Uma lenda local conta que, quando o Deus da criação estava criando o mundo e distribuindo suas riquezas, ao chegar à Iacútia teve as mãos entorpecidas pelo frio deixando cair lá todas as riquezas. A cidade possui escritórios de muitas empresas de mineração, incluindo ALROSA, cujas minas de diamante na Iacútia somam cerca de 20% da produção mundial de diamante bruto. A cidade de Iacutusque é a sede do Estádio Tuymaada e do extinto clube de futebol FC Iakutia, que já participou do Campeonato Russo de Futebol.

Якутск один из самых быстрорастущих по населению городов России[6]: с 1980 по 2025 год численность его жителей увеличилась более чем в два раза. Якутск был основан в 1632 году казаками и первоначально назывался Ленским или Якутским острогом. Со временем за поселением закрепилось название Якутский острог, в 1708 году оно получило статус города и имя Якутский, позже превратившееся в Якутск[7]. Так как город расположен чуть севернее 62° северной широты, в летнее время здесь наблюдается длительный период «белых ночей», а в декабре светлое время суток длится всего 3-4 часа. И это единственный из крупных городов России (с населением больше 300 тысяч человек), не имеющих круглогодичного наземного сообщения с федеральной дорожной сетью[8].
